data.reasoning: The package is a standard -bin AUR package that downloads a prebuilt binary from the project's own GitHub releases (github.com/subnix-work/tinox) with a pinned SHA256 checksum. The PKGBUILD contains only static variable definitions and a package() function that installs files without any network access, code execution, or obfuscation. The .SRCINFO and .gitignore are standard metadata files with no executable content. The checksum pinning closes the artifact swap risk.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was triggered by qwen3-235b returning 'inconclusive' due to HTTP 400 API errors during file review, not due to security concerns. Notably, the same model's initial PKGBUILD audit (before the full review) succeeded and found it SAFE. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The openrouter/free report is advisory-only and doesn't count as a vote. The 'disagreement' is therefore an artifact of API failures, not genuine security uncertainty.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to complete full file review due to HTTP 400 errors on PKGBUILD and .gitignore, resulting in inconclusive verdict despite successful initial PKGBUILD audit
learnings: When an initial PKGBUILD audit succeeds but subsequent file reviews fail with API errors, the tool should not override the successful initial finding with 'inconclusive' - it should either retry or preserve the partial verdict
API errors (HTTP 400, timeouts, crashes) should be tracked separately from security inconclusiveness to avoid triggering unnecessary escalation audits
For -bin packages with pinned checksums from official upstream sources, models correctly identify the swap risk as closed - this pattern is well-understood
